 Oral Order
1.

The petitioneraccused No. 6, who has been chargesheeted for offences punishable under
Sections 406, 420, 504, and 506 read with Section 34 of the Ipc, is before this Court.
2.  The prosecution alleges that the complainant's father was a member of the Binnypete Nivasigala Seva Sangha and had subscribed to membership by paying  10,000 for the allotment of a site in 1988.
Similarly, 413 persons applied for membership, with each member paying  10,000 to the Sangha for site allotment.

After many of the original office bearers of the Sangha had expired,
accused Nos. 1 to 3, along with others, reregistered the Sangha and obtained a bulk allotment NC:
2025:KHC:10262 from the Bengaluru Development Authority (BDA).

Instead of allotting the sites claimed under this bulk allotment, accused Nos. 1 to 3, as office bearers of the Sangha, conveyed the subject site in favor of petitioneraccused No. 6 by executing a registered Sale Deed dated 11.05.2018.
When the complainant and other chargesheet witnesses approached the Sangha to question this transaction, the office bearers abused them and threatened them with dire consequences.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned HCGP for Respondent No. 1 - State, and the learned counsel for Respondent No. 2.

sentences.text: A perusal of the chargesheet material indicates that the complainant and the other chargesheet witnesses were allegedly members of the Sangha who paid  10,000 each between 1988 and 1992.
The Sangha executed a registered Sale Deed in favor of the petitioner on 07.05.2018.

The petitioner is neither an office bearer of the Sangha nor does he have any authority to allot sites to its members;
he is merely a bona fide purchaser who acquired the subject site through a registered Sale Deed.

Whether the complainant and the other NC: 2025:KHC:10262 chargesheet witnesses are entitled to an allotment is a matter to be adjudicated before the appropriate forum and cannot be addressed in a criminal proceeding.

Moreover, there is no allegation that the petitioner colluded with the office bearers of the Sangha to deprive the complainant and the other witnesses of their alleged legitimate right to an allotment.
Therefore, the essential elements constituting the commission of the offences alleged against the petitioner are conspicuously absent.
Under such circumstances, the continuation of the criminal proceedings would be an abuse of the process of law.

5. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal Petition is allowed.
 ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.
 No.6013/2023 on the file of IV  Additional CMM Court, Bengaluru City insofar as it relates to accused No.6 is hereby quashed.
iii) The Trial Court shall proceed against other accused persons in accordance with law without being influenced by any NC: 2025:KHC:10262 observation made in this order and the observation made hereinabove is only for the purpose of present petition.

Sd/-
(HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR) JUDGE BS Sri. Inder Kumar vs State Of Karnataka on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18102126/
